analysis: Both supplied units are base_text excerpts of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (base lines 1-860). No patch hunks or head_text were supplied, so the actual PR delta is not visible. Coverage is therefore limited and I cannot tell what changed. The file is documentation only, so no executable security behavior changes from the file itself. The base text documents several security-relevant contracts that later passes should compare against any head change. (1) Logout, lines 441-480: the process is stopped and its exit confirmed before revocation. The bearer token is sent only to the recorded issuer via POST /v1/device/revoke, with no redirects and a 10 s timeout. Only HTTP 204 confirms revocation, and local deletion proceeds regardless (A-008, TB-011, T-053). (2) Enroll, lines 548-562: on macOS 27+ the output is guidance only and grants no authorization (T-052). (3) Cache, lines 18-40: the `cache set --directory` description of payload location, volume UUID pinning and the SSD cache is relevant to T-041. The doc says these checks do not certify disk firmware. (4) Switch and autopilot sections: model selection and consent semantics. Later passes should check that any head edit does not overclaim these controls. Examples would be calling local logout remote invalidation, treating the enrollment guidance as App Attest authorization, or implying that cache storage checks give freshness or firmware attestation. They should also check that backend claims stay platform-owned and that no new commands or flags are documented without matching threat-model coverage. No findings are reported because no changed lines were visible.
